skill.name: tmux
skill.description: Control isolated tmux sessions for AI assisted development tasks, background commands, interactive tools, and local service monitoring.
skill.summary: Create, monitor, capture, and clean up tmux sessions from AI development workflows.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in documentation and examples are false positives from Markdown code spans, template literals, or sample installation paths. The confirmed risks are the intended local tmux command execution, pane capture, and session management capabilities. Additional review found local metadata exposure in predictable temp storage and missing confirmation for destructive actions.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary local commands can be launched through tmux sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before creating sessions from generated commands, and show the exact command before execution.

remediation.issue: Session metadata is stored in predictable temp paths and includes command strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use a user-private directory with 0700 permissions and write the session store with 0600 permissions.

remediation.issue: Destructive kill and cleanup commands do not enforce confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Add an interactive confirmation flag or require an explicit force option for non-interactive destructive operations.

remediation.issue: Regex wait helpers accept unrestricted patterns over large captured output.
remediation.suggestion: Offer fixed-string mode by default, cap history lines, and document regex performance risks.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable Temp Session Store Exposes Command Metadata
semantic_findings.description: The default session store is under /tmp and records session command strings. On shared systems, weak directory permissions could expose commands or allow local tampering.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code defines /tmp based storage and writes the serialized session map. The documentation shows that command strings are part of the stored session data.

semantic_findings.title: User Controlled Regex Over Captured Terminal Output
semantic_findings.description: The wait helpers compile or pass user supplied patterns over captured pane text. Complex patterns can cause expensive matching against large terminal output.

content.user_title: Manage Tmux Sessions from AI Workflows
content.value_statement: Long-running terminal tasks are hard to supervise from AI tools. This skill creates isolated tmux sessions, monitors output, and cleans up sessions when work is complete.
actual_capabilities: Creates tmux sessions for tasks, services, and agent workflows.
Sends literal keystrokes to managed tmux panes.
Captures recent pane output for status checks and logs.
Lists, syncs, attaches to, and kills managed sessions.
Provides helper scripts to find sessions and wait for text.
limitations: Requires tmux, Bun, and Bash on the local machine.
Runs local commands with the current user permissions.
Does not provide remote tmux access or cloud orchestration.
Session metadata is stored on the local filesystem.

use_cases.title: Monitor Builds
use_cases.description: Run builds or test suites in tmux and check progress without blocking the AI session.

use_cases.title: Run Local Services
use_cases.description: Start development servers in managed sessions and capture logs while debugging local applications.

use_cases.title: Control Interactive Tools
use_cases.description: Drive REPLs, shells, and other terminal tools by sending input and reading pane output.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for one background command.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tmux task named build for my project build command, then show me how to monitor it.

prompt_templates.title: Check Progress
prompt_templates.scenario: Review output from an existing session.
prompt_templates.prompt: List managed tmux sessions, identify the active build or test task, and summarize its latest output.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep a local service running while work continues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Start my local development server in a tmux service session, wait until it reports ready, and keep it running.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced session management across several tasks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Sync tmux state, capture outputs from stale sessions, then ask before killing any session that may still be useful.

output_examples.input: Start a long test run and let me keep working.
output_examples.output: Created a managed tmux task, reported the session name, and provided monitoring instructions.

output_examples.input: Check whether the server is ready.
output_examples.output: Captured recent pane output, detected the ready message, and summarized the service status.
Reviewed managed sessions, identified inactive entries, and removed the selected stale sessions.

best_practices: Use clear session names that describe the task or service.
Review captured output before stopping long-running sessions.
Keep socket and session storage in a user-private directory.
anti_patterns: Do not run untrusted commands without reviewing them first.
Do not store secrets in command strings or terminal output.
Do not leave unused service sessions running indefinitely.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages local tmux sessions for commands, services, and interactive terminal tools.

faq.question: Does it require tmux?
faq.answer: Yes. The local machine must have tmux installed and available on the PATH.

faq.question: Can it run arbitrary commands?
faq.answer: Yes. Commands run locally with the permissions of the current user.

faq.question: Can I inspect output later?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can capture recent pane output from a managed tmux session.

faq.question: Does it use my normal tmux socket?
faq.answer: It uses a private socket path by default to reduce conflicts with personal tmux sessions.

faq.question: What should I protect?
faq.answer: Protect session storage and avoid placing secrets in commands or terminal output.
